subsystems.name: Annular combustor
subsystems.role: the ring-shaped channel where the detonation wave circulates continuously.

subsystems.name: Injector plate
subsystems.role: feeds propellant fast enough and uniformly enough to sustain a wave that consumes mixture in microseconds.
parts: valving or fluidic barriers to stop back-flow

subsystems.name: Ignition and initiation system
subsystems.role: creates the first detonation that then self-sustains.

subsystems.name: Cooling system
subsystems.role: removes heat from walls exposed to detonation pressures and temperatures.

subsystems.name: Nozzle and exhaust
subsystems.role: turns the unsteady, high-pressure exhaust into useful thrust.

subsystems.name: Instrumentation and control
subsystems.role: measures wave speed, pressure and temperature to detect mode changes and instability.

buildSteps.title: Choose propellant pair
buildSteps.detail: The mixture must detonate readily; hydrogen–oxygen and methane–oxygen are common choices, and some concepts add a liquid for density.

buildSteps.title: Design the annulus
buildSteps.detail: The ring's diameter and gap are set so that one or more waves circulate at the intended frequency, typically a few kilohertz.

buildSteps.title: Make the chamber
buildSteps.detail: The contoured inner and outer walls are often 3D-printed in copper alloy so the cooling passages can be printed inside the metal.

buildSteps.title: Build the injector
buildSteps.detail: Hundreds or thousands of orifices are drilled or printed to inject propellant at the right angles and velocities; the hardest part is preventing the wave pressure from pushing hot gas back up the feed lines.

buildSteps.title: Fit ignition and diagnostics
buildSteps.detail: A small pre-detonator initiates the wave; pressure transducers around the ring record its passage.

buildSteps.title: Fire in short bursts
buildSteps.detail: Ground tests run for fractions of a second to a few seconds, capturing thrust, wave count and heat load before anything melts.

buildSteps.title: Close the cooling loop
buildSteps.detail: Regenerative cooling using the propellant itself is tested until the chamber can run progressively longer.

buildSteps.title: Integrate a nozzle
buildSteps.detail: The exhaust is expanded through a nozzle designed for unsteady, rotating flow rather than steady combustion.

buildSteps.title: Scale and flight-test
buildSteps.detail: The engine is enlarged, then flown on a test vehicle to prove it works under real acceleration and vibration.

prerequisites.why: predicting how many waves form, and keeping that number steady, is still largely empirical.
only 3D printing can build the intricate internal cooling channels and injector geometries inside a copper chamber.
feed systems must respond in microseconds and withstand detonation back-pressure.
walls face repeated detonation pressure spikes and heat fluxes that shorten hardware life.
reliable ignition without a large pre-detonator remains a design constraint.

pathway.milestone: bench tests of annular detonation chambers running for a few seconds; a 3D-printed rocket detonation chamber was test-fired by NASA around 2022
pathway.unlocks: data on wave behaviour, thrust and cooling at realistic scale.

pathway.milestone: reusable upper-stage or in-space engine demonstrators with measured performance gain
pathway.unlocks: a niche where mass and efficiency matter more than long burn life.

pathway.milestone: air-breathing detonation concepts for high-speed flight
pathway.unlocks: compact, high-efficiency propulsion for hypersonic vehicles.
lighter launch vehicles and more payload per kilogram of propellant, if cooling and lifetime are solved.
